title: Grace, Triumphant in the Throne
description: Grace, Triumphant in the Throne in Tonic Solfa to MESSIAH (HERALD), doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 75, “Not of works”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MESSIAH (HERALD); any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Grace, tri-um-phant in the throne, Scorns a ri-val, reigns a-lone! Come and bow be-neath her sway, Cast your i-dol works a-way: Works of man, when made his plea, Nev-er shall ac-cept-ed be; Fruits of pride (vain glo-rious worm) Are the best he can per-form.

lines: Come and bow beneath her sway,
Works of man, when made his plea,
Are the best he can perform.
Self, the god his soul adores,
But when God the Judge shall come,
Then for rocks and hills to hide,
All his works and all his pride.
What the worthy and the wise,
But the grace that never can.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to MESSIAH (HERALD) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
